**Built 2026-10-29; cherry-picked the same day to local tsd-enterprise master (906752ee3e after squashing, on unpushed a22082b0cb) and local jusprin-newui (30ae01eae0, one commit: chat_key plumbing copied byte-for-byte from a08d17471f without prompt_cache_key, plus the header).** Originally (branches and worktrees deleted 2026-10-29 after squashing): gateway on tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-chat-capture` (6d10075718, worktree `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/chat-capture`, tests via docker compose project `chat-capture` with a ports-reset override; obico-server submodule must be at eb0f29c3 there). App header on JusPrin `claude/chat-uid-header` (on `claude/chat-history-cache`). Chat id = sha256(`<projectId>/<conversationId>`)[:32], not a stored chatUid. Trimming removal and the context-limit rule belong to the chat-history-cache programme (R3a done, R3b pending), not to this work.

Kenneth's decisions (2026-10-29):
- **Chat id:** the app sends its own random `chatUid` in an `X-JusPrin-Chat` header. The turn id (`<project>-<conversation>-<message>-attempt-n`) can't be split reliably, because conversation ids are `c-1` and restart per project.
- **No trimming:** the app removes history trimming, so the newest request of a chat is the whole chat.
- **Buffered saves:** keep the newest request plus its reply per chat in Redis, and have a Celery beat task write it to GCS once the chat is quiet. Kenneth called saving every request "pretty dumb".
- **Consent:** opt-out was decided, then removed the same day (folded into 906752ee3e): keep every chat; sharing for a reward is arranged case by case. No account field or toggle. Account deletion still deletes kept chats.
- **Retention:** kept until the person deletes their account; no age limit.
- **Blind write, no branches (2026-11-02):** `_keep_sync` stores the request and reply events as raw text, and a retry, edit or revert overwrites the earlier version. Kenneth chose this over keeping branch files, knowing rejected attempts are lost. `[json.loads(data) for data in self.events]` had thrown on OpenRouter's `data: [DONE]`, losing every Standard chat. Commit 7c69f331be on tsd-enterprise `claude/credits-ledger`, not pushed as of 2026-11-02. The design doc's Branches section is out of date.

State on 2026-11-02: 906752ee3e is on origin/master and origin/release. No deployment's `env` on the clusters names `JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER`, and neither does the ops repo, so capture looks off; a value from a secret via `envFrom` was not checked.

**Why:** Kenneth wants the stored chats usable as fine-tuning data later.

**How to apply:**
- Still open: a legal read on the vendor terms. Anthropic's and OpenAI's terms forbid training competing models on their output.
- The privacy policy (last updated 2022-04-05) has to be updated and people notified before capture starts.
- Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]].

Since 2026-10-30 (commit "Stop naming Orca to the model...") the app keeps each request sent in `<data dir>/jusprin/request-log/*.json`, newest 200, pictures replaced by their size, no headers, no responses or reasoning (Kenneth said no reasoning). Read that first; the steps below are only for chats from before it.

The app did not save what it sent to the model. To replay an older turn, rebuild it:

- Running build: first line of `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/log/debug_*.log.0` names the commit. Read `ProviderAgent.cpp`, `ResponsesCodec.cpp` and `AgentHost.cpp` at that commit, since the wire shape changed in b08a307459 (append-only record).
- Chat: `jusprin/projects/<id>/current-state.json`, `state.conversations[n]` (messages, `chatModel`, `plan`) and `state.toolActivities` (arguments and results, joined by `correlationId` to the message that made the call).
- Workspace block: `resumeCheckpoint.summary` holds it, including `sliceWarnings`; it is saved at the end of the turn, so check it matches the turn replayed.
- Left out of the wire: note messages, and the workspace block of earlier user messages. A note-started turn sends a user message holding only the workspace block.
- A fired skill goes only on its own request (`newest_once`), never on later requests of that turn. print-issues fires by itself on the first request after a slice with new warnings, not only on a chip press.
- Cannot be recovered: reasoning items from the turn's earlier responses, and a skill's picture.

content.text:
The model offered "Save preset" on its own. Nothing in its instructions says that unsaved preset edits are normal and stay with the project. When you then picked "Save preset & slice", the app refused the save. The model told you three times to tap a Save preset card, and that card was never drawn. I worked this out from the app's own record of the chat, the last request it sent in `/tmp/JusPrin2-stg/jusprin/request-log/` plus the project's `current-state.json`. I changed no code.

**Why the model brought up saving**

- The edit itself worked. After `settings_apply_patch` changed walls, infill, alternate extra wall and vertical shell thickness, the result came back with `presetDirty: true` and `savedAs: ""`.
- The tool's description presents `persistAs` as the way to save, and says "Without persistAs a change stays unsaved." The model took "unsaved" to mean unfinished work, so it offered to save.
- Nothing the model reads says what an unsaved edit means for the person. The edit is kept with this project and used when slicing. It is dropped when another project opens. Its reason, "so it doesn't affect future projects", has it backwards: an unsaved edit already can't reach another project, and saving is what would carry it over.
- I found no rule in your words that the agent must never offer a save. The rule from 2026-10-24, decided for calibration, covers how a save happens: the agent only previews, and the person saves from a card. It doesn't say whether the agent should offer one. JusPrin made that rule apply to every project chat (`m_saves_need_approval` in `AgentHost.cpp`). Only the calibration skill tells the model about it.

**Why there was no card to tap**

1. You picked "Save preset & slice". The model previewed the same four changes with `persistAs`. The edits were already applied, so the preview found no differences and listed every key as `unchanged`.
2. `settings_proposal` (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:463`) returns nothing when no change is listed, so no card was drawn. In `current-state.json`, that preview's entry has no `proposal`.
3. The model then called `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs`. The app refused it with "your settings_preview_patch with persistAs shows them a card with Save preset" (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:956`). In this order of events, that message is false.
4. The model believed the message and kept pointing you at the card.

Both texts are the same on `jusprin-newui`, so this isn't specific to the byoai-newui worktree. The chat ran on JusPrin Cloud's `slicer-basic` model.

**What I propose (not built):**
- **Guidance:** tell the model, in `settings_apply_patch`'s description or its result, that an unsaved edit is kept with this project and used for slicing, and that it should offer to save a preset only when the person wants to reuse the settings elsewhere.
- **Card:** make the save card work after an edit has already been applied. Either the preview compares against the saved preset rather than the current values, or the refusal message stops promising a card that won't appear.

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).

content.text:
Mostly yes. JusPrin's own screens never call a preset edit "unsaved" or ask the person to save one. The setting stays with the project. OrcaSlicer's settings window still shows the old marker, and the model still gets the old flag. There is no separate save tool: saving a preset is the `persistAs` option on `settings_apply_patch`. You declined screen access to the running app, so all of this comes from reading the code. I didn't see it on screen.

**How JusPrin presents edited settings**

- **Setup card:** it says something like "0.20mm Standard with Generic PLA. 4 settings differ from the presets." It never says "unsaved" (`SetupCard.tsx`, `presetsLine`).
- **All settings panel:** an edited setting is in bold with "Preset: 2" under it, and there's a "Changed" filter. It has no Save button.
- **Opening another project:** JusPrin first saves the open project to its version history, edits included. Then it drops the edits without OrcaSlicer's "unsaved changes" prompt (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::release_project`). Switching presets through the agent drops them the same way and lists what was dropped.
- **Status row:** with autosave on, it shows "Saving…", "Saved" or "Couldn't save". It isn't about presets.

**Where the old concept still shows**

- **OrcaSlicer's settings window:** "Printer settings" in the printer menu and the matching filament row open it. It still has OrcaSlicer's "(modified)" marker and its Save icon.
- **Filament chip:** picking a filament there calls OrcaSlicer's `Tab::select_preset`. I'd expect OrcaSlicer's "transfer or discard your changes" prompt when the old filament has edits. I didn't run it to check.
- **What the model reads:** `presetDirty`, `savedAs`, the "Without persistAs a change stays unsaved" text, and warnings like `saves_unsaved_edits`. The model still lives in OrcaSlicer's world of dirty and saved presets. That's why it worried about saving and offered "Save preset".

**Do we have a tool to save a user preset?**

There's no dedicated one. `presets_save` was folded into the `persistAs` option of `settings_apply_patch`. Called with a name, it saves the edited preset under that name, using OrcaSlicer's own Save. A preset that ships with the app can only be saved as a copy. Who may save depends on where the model runs:

- **Project chat (yours):** the app refuses the agent's save. The agent has to call `settings_preview_patch` with `persistAs`. That draws a card with a Save preset button, and the person presses it. This was built for calibration results on 2026-10-24 and applies to every project chat.
- **Printer chat and filament chat:** the agent saves directly. The filament chat even refuses an edit that isn't saved, because its edits would vanish when the chat closes.
- **Outside MCP clients:** they save directly.

So in a project chat, nothing tells the model that saving is the exception. The only words about saving are the tool description's, and they read as if saving were the normal last step.

It's a fair suspect, but I can't call it the most likely one yet. The model's words, "The preset now has unsaved changes", are a close match for `presetDirty: true`. But two other things the model read in that chat also say "unsaved" or invite a save, and nothing I have shows which one moved it:

- **The result field:** `settings_apply_patch` returned `presetDirty: true` and `savedAs: ""`.
- **The description of `persistAs`:** "Save the changed preset under this name… Without persistAs a change stays unsaved." The model read this on every request. Of the three, it's the one that offers saving as an action.
- **The tool's own description:** "With persistAs the preset is saved as well, and savedAs names what it was saved as."

I can't test it against that exact chat anymore. Your launch command starts with `rm -rf "$D"`, so relaunching the app wiped `/tmp/JusPrin2-stg`, including the request log I read earlier.

**Who reads `presetDirty`**

No app code reads it. The Agent page, the printer chat and the filament chat never look at it. The only readers are:
- the models: the project chat, the printer and filament chats, and any outside MCP client such as Claude Desktop.
- two test assertions in `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` (lines 234 and 1858), and the fake results in the printer and project prompt test scripts.

It also tells a model nothing it needs. After a save, `savedAs` already names the saved preset. Without a save, the field just repeats that the change wasn't saved. Removing it means deleting it from the result in `ToolResults.cpp` and from the declared output schema in `ToolRegistry.cpp`, and updating those tests. Outside MCP clients receive the schema and the result together, so nothing breaks for them.

Two neighbours carry the same idea, and I'd look at them in the same pass. `workspace_inspect` sends a `presetsDirty` field in its project section. `printer_setup_preview` sends an `unsavedEdits` list. That list does matter, though: it says which edits a switch would drop.

**Decision needed: remove the field, and measure whether that stops the save offer?**

The removal is cheap and safe, whether or not it's the cause. Measuring is what tells us whether removing it is enough, or whether the `persistAs` wording also has to change. The test I'd run uses the project prompt test harness (`tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`). Its saved chats include a settings apply that returns `presetDirty: true`. I'd run that turn about 10 times each, three ways: as it is today, without the field, and without the field plus a reworded `persistAs` description. Then I'd count how often the reply offers to save a preset. That's around 30 paid model calls, and your rule is that I ask before spending on live runs. Your options:

- **Remove it and measure (my pick).** Costs the 30 calls, and we learn which text matters.
- **Just remove it.** Costs nothing, but if the description is the real cause, the model will keep offering saves.

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered, with one
  exception below.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

Two kinds of change are ever answered, each only in a case that says so
(`later`), because what matters there is what the model does next: a
`setup_record` with a plan and no purpose (`print-this-no-purpose` and
`print-hook-no-purpose`), and a `slice_start` (`print-hook-no-purpose`). `later`
maps what the run has done so far to the point recorded right after it, by a
## Running it

The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 81 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

A run ends with every case it ran beside the baseline (below). It exits 1
when a case is marked worse, 2 when nothing was judged (there is no baseline,
or the run's model, host or judge differs from the baseline's), 0 otherwise;
`--must-pass N` makes the exit code 1 when a case passes fewer than N runs
instead, as before baselines.
`--results FILE` also saves the run's counts in the baseline's form, and
`--compare FILE` prints a saved run beside the baseline again without sending
anything.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Request bodies as posted (`--request-log`)

`--request-log DIR` (with `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent`,
`--plan-journey` or `--project-prompt-requests`; `DIR` must be new or empty) writes each request
the project chat's Agent posts as `NNNN-request.json`, byte for byte, and
beside it `NNNN-usage.txt`: the project and chat id on the first line, then
each usage object of the response stream. `python3
tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py DIR` prints, for consecutive bodies of
one chat, the first differing byte and its JSON path; `--ignore-cache-control`
drops Anthropic's moving cache breakpoint first. JusPrin writes JSON keys in
sorted order, so on the Responses API `input` comes before `instructions` and
`tools`: a clean append shows up as `$.input[n]`, and a change in
`instructions` or `tools` after it is not reported. Tests: the Catch2
`[request-log]` case and `python3 -m unittest
tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge
  (`baseline.json`), except the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's
  own (`baseline-claude-cli.json`, which `--backend claude-cli` compares with).
  A claude-cli count is compared only with that one. Changing the judge
  changes what every judged case counts, so the runner will not compare a
  run on another judge with either: such results start their own baseline,
  under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 29 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.

  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load

  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the

content.text:
I removed `presetDirty` from `settings_apply_patch`'s result, and all 563 agent tests pass. In the replays, removing the field made the model call a change "unsaved" less often. The reworded tool text brought that to zero. The samples are small, though, so neither result is proven. Nothing is committed yet. The work is in my own worktree, `.claude/worktrees/drop-preset-dirty`, on branch `claude/drop-preset-dirty`, cut from `jusprin-dev`.

**What changed**
- The result no longer includes `presetDirty`, and the tool's declared output schema drops it too (`ToolResults.cpp`, `ToolRegistry.cpp`).
- `test_tool_coordinator.cpp` now checks that the field is absent. I put the field back for one build to confirm the tests catch it: the output-schema check failed. I then restored the file, and the full suite passes again.
- The fake result in the printer prompt test no longer sends the field.
- The project prompt test's saved chats (`requests.json`) had the field in three recorded results. I deleted it by hand instead of re-recording. Re-recording needs the full app harness build, and the machine was at a load of 30 to 44 on 12 cores.
- `mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` says the field is gone, why, and what the replays showed.

**What the replays show**

I used the saved test chat where the person asks to "set layer height to 0.28" and the change has just been applied. The model was DeepSeek V4 Flash, the same model staging's "slicer-basic" points to, so it's the model from your chat. Then I read every reply.

| Version | Calls the change "unsaved" | Offers to save a preset |
|---|---|---|
| As recorded, with `presetDirty: true` | 3 of 10 | 1 of 10 |
| Field removed | 1 of 9 | 1 of 9 |
| Field removed, tool text reworded | 0 of 9 | 0 of 9 |

In the last two rows, one run each called `setup_record` instead of replying, so 9 replies were read.

Typical replies from the first row: "This change is unsaved — it'll stay until you switch presets or close the project." and "Want me to save this as a new preset, or keep it as-is for now?" The run that offered a save without the field said: "if you want to keep this setting permanently, let me know and I can save it as a new preset."

What this means:
- The trend fits your guess, but 3 of 10 against 1 of 9 is too few runs to call the field the cause.
- Save offers came up in only 1 run per 10 in this chat, so 10 runs can't tell the versions apart on that count. Your chat was a strength change ahead of a print, which this test chat doesn't cover.
- One run of the reworded version got a fact right that the old text never gives: "saved with the project (not saved as a process preset, so other projects keep their own settings)."

**The rewording (tried, not applied)**

This would go into the descriptions of `persistAs` and `settings_apply_patch`:

> Without persistAs the change is part of this project: it is kept with the project and used when it slices, and the person has nothing to save. Save a preset only when the person wants these settings for other projects. A preset other than the one being edited changes only by being saved.

**Spend**

40 runs instead of the 30 you approved. The runner cuts each reply to its first 160 characters, and the part about saving came later in the replies. So I lifted the limit locally and ran the as-recorded version a second time. Each request was about 14,000 input tokens, almost all cached.

**Still open**
- **Saved chat after the wording change:** if the wording goes in, `project_tools.json` has to be regenerated from `ToolRegistry.cpp`.
- **Missing Save preset card:** the model promised a card that never appeared, because a preview of changes that are already applied draws none. That's a separate fix and isn't touched here.
Repeat what you said in plain English under 100 words.

I took the "unsaved" flag out of the settings tool's result. All the tests pass, and nothing is committed yet.

Then I replayed a saved chat where someone changes the layer height, 10 times for each version:

- **With the flag:** the AI called the change "unsaved" in 3 of 10 replies.
- **Without the flag:** 1 of 9 replies did.
- **Without the flag, plus clearer wording in the tool's description:** none of 9 did.

So removing the flag helps, and the clearer wording helps more. With this few runs, it isn't proof. Offers to save a preset came up too rarely in this chat to measure.
No, the result is good enough. Commit the flag removal and the workding change
